observation_summary: The application throws an OutOfMemoryError when performing curve fitting with a large number of points. The stack trace indicates that a large n x n matrix is being allocated in memory during the optimization process.
hypothesis: The optimization process incorrectly assumes that a weight matrix must be represented as a full n x n matrix, even when the weights are provided as a simple vector. This leads to an unnecessary O(n^2) memory allocation, which causes heap exhaustion for large datasets.
prediction: The fix will involve changing the representation of the weight matrix from a full n x n matrix to a more memory-efficient structure (like a DiagonalMatrix) when the input is a vector, avoiding the creation of the massive n x n array.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace points directly to the allocation of a large matrix in DiagonalMatrix.getData() and TriDiagonalTransformer.<init>, which are called during the optimization setup. The bug report explicitly states that an n x n matrix is created when only an n-element vector is needed, confirming the algorithmic inefficiency.
reasoning_summary: The issue is an inefficient computational strategy (Algorithm/Method) where the system forces a full matrix representation for what should be a diagonal operation. This is not a missing check (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment/Initialization), or a design capability gap (Function/Class/Object), but rather an implementation choice in the algorithm that fails to scale for large inputs.
evidence_used: Bug report description: 'When using the Weigth class to pass a large number of weights to multivariate vector optimizers, an nxn full matrix is created (and copied) when a n elements vector is used.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The capability to perform optimization exists; the issue is the inefficient implementation of the weight matrix handling, not a missing feature or design capability.
The issue is not a single wrong value or initialization, but the choice of an inefficient data structure and algorithm for handling the weight matrix.
